Subjective

History of Present Illness (HPI):
- 58-year-old male with left lower extremity radicular pain in the L5 distribution for 10 weeks, rated 7/10, limiting walking and sleep. Completed 6 weeks of physical therapy and home exercise program with minimal relief. Trial of gabapentin with partial relief. No prior epidural steroid injections.

Past medical history:
- Hyperlipidemia.

Relevant surgeries/procedures:
- None reported.

Medications:
- Gabapentin 300 mg by mouth three times daily. Atorvastatin 20 mg by mouth daily.

Social History:
- Works as a delivery driver. Never smoker.

Objective

Physical Examination:
- Musculoskeletal: Positive straight leg raise on the left at 40 degrees.
- Neurological: Diminished sensation in the left L5 dermatome. Strength 4/5 in left ankle dorsiflexion; otherwise 5/5 in bilateral lower extremities.

Assessment & Plan

Assessment and Plan:
1. Lumbar radiculopathy, left L5
   - MRI lumbar spine 2026-08-14 shows left paracentral disc protrusion at L4-L5 contacting the traversing L5 nerve root
   - Proceed with left L4-L5 transforaminal epidural steroid injection
   - Continue home exercise program

Follow-up:
- Return to clinic two weeks after the injection

Procedures scheduled: left L4-L5 transforaminal epidural steroid injection
